title: Grade 6 French — Fri, Jun 20
description: La nourriture — Day 5 of 5: Week review — menu reading and food dialogue
subject: french

questions.question: A menu shows: Entrée: salade verte — 4€. Plat: poulet rôti — 12€. What is the total cost?
Which article correctly completes: 'Je mange ___ riz' (rice — masculine)?
questions.explanation: Le riz is masculine and starts with a consonant, so we use 'du'. Je mange du riz = I eat some rice.

questions.question: Read the dialogue: Serveur: 'Vous désirez?' Client: 'Je voudrais ___.' What is the client doing?
questions.explanation: Je voudrais + food item = ordering food. The client is responding to the waiter's 'What would you like?'

questions.question: Which sentence means 'I prefer vegetables to meat'?
options: J'aime la viande plus les légumes.
Je préfère les légumes à la viande.
J'adore la viande et les légumes.
Je déteste la viande comme les légumes.
questions.explanation: Je préfère X à Y = I prefer X to Y. Je préfère les légumes à la viande = I prefer vegetables to meat.

questions.question: In negation, 'Je mange du pain' becomes:
options: Je ne mange pas du pain.
Je ne mange pas de pain.
Je ne mange pas le pain.
Je ne mange pas des pains.
questions.explanation: In negation, du/de la/des all become 'de'. Je ne mange pas de pain = I don't eat (any) bread.

questions.question: What does the waiter mean when he says 'Et comme dessert?'
options: What would you like as a starter?
questions.explanation: Comme dessert = for dessert. Et comme dessert? = And for dessert? The waiter is asking about the final course.

questions.question: Which phrase correctly says 'a cup of tea, please'?
options: Un verre de thé, s'il vous plaît.
Une tasse de thé, s'il vous plaît.
Une bouteille de thé, s'il vous plaît.
Un bol de thé, s'il vous plaît.
questions.explanation: Une tasse = a cup. Une tasse de thé = a cup of tea. Un verre = glass, une bouteille = bottle.

questions.question: A student says 'J'adore les fruits mais je déteste les légumes.' What does this mean?
options: I like vegetables but I hate fruits.
I love fruits but I hate vegetables.
questions.explanation: J'adore = I love, je déteste = I hate, mais = but. J'adore les fruits mais je déteste les légumes = I love fruits but I hate vegetables.

questions.question: Complete: 'Il boit ___ jus d'orange.' (jus = masculine, starts with consonant)
questions.explanation: Le jus is masculine and starts with a consonant, so we use 'du'. Il boit du jus d'orange = He drinks some orange juice.

questions.question: Which French food word means 'bread'?
questions.explanation: Le pain = bread. Le gâteau = cake, le riz = rice, la tarte = tart/pie.

questions.question: How do you politely say 'Could I have the menu?'
options: Je voudrais la carte, s'il vous plaît.
questions.explanation: Je voudrais + s'il vous plaît is the polite form. Je voudrais la carte, s'il vous plaît = I would like the menu, please.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the partitive with a vowel?
questions.explanation: L'huile (oil) starts with a silent h (= vowel sound), so we use 'de l''. Je mange de l'huile = I eat some oil.

questions.question: Waiter: 'C'est tout?' Customer wants to say 'Yes, that's all.' Which is correct?
questions.explanation: C'est tout = that's all / that's everything. Oui, c'est tout = Yes, that's all.

questions.question: Which word is the French equivalent of 'delicious'?
questions.explanation: Délicieux (masc.) / délicieuse (fem.) = delicious. Dégoûtant = disgusting, froid = cold, chaud = hot.

questions.question: A customer says 'Nous sommes quatre.' What is the waiter likely to do next?
questions.explanation: Nous sommes quatre = We are four (people). The waiter will likely find a table for four and bring four menus.
